title: The Carter emotional relationships
goal: A reader can trace the Carter family across three generations and identify the cutoff, enmeshment, and conflict without confusing emotional connections with ancestry or marriage.

rubric.must: Arthur and Ruth occupy the top generation row and connect as Michael's parents; Michael and Claire occupy the middle row and connect as the parents of Anna, Ben, and Grace on the bottom row.
A broken emotional line with a visible gap joins Arthur to Anna across the middle generation, and the legend identifies its pattern as cutoff.
Three parallel emotional lines join Ruth to Michael, and the legend identifies this pattern as fused or enmeshed.
A zigzag emotional line with hash marks joins Michael to Grace, and the legend identifies its pattern as conflict.

Marriage bars and parent-child branches remain individually traceable as solid family lines, visually distinct from all three emotional patterns; emotional crossings do not appear to create extra spouses or children.
No emotional line passes through a person's symbol or label, and the two people joined by each emotional line can be identified without following a family line.
Every person's name and birth year is readable without overlapping another label, and Anna's double index outline is visible.

ideal.notes: Arthur and Ruth are the parents of Michael, whose partnership with Claire connects to Anna, Ben and Grace; Anna carries the index outline. Separate smooth gutter arcs identify Arthur–Anna cutoff, Ruth–Michael three-line fusion and Michael–Grace zigzag conflict with hash marks, distinct from the solid family branches.
